concerns: All three r2 findings are repaired and no new defect is proposed. Recheck method for the record: wc -w on drafts/ch21.md returns 5,290 against the ceiling of 5,290; diff -u drafts/ch21-r2.md drafts/ch21.md returns seven changed lines and nothing else (21, 33, 169 = the findings; 61, 157, 173, 205 = the declared trims); a file-wide grep for 'bow|bolt|span|stirrup' returns hits only at 111, 167, 169, 173, 191 and 205, all of which refer to the same single weapon.

Taste only: at line 111 Seln is 'on the coping already, ten strides along, with the bow in his hand', and the bow's provenance arrives fifty-eight lines later at 169 ('laid on the coping when he went down to give Karis a shoulder, and which Seln had taken up'). The pickup itself is never staged, so a reader who tries to time it has to assume Seln took it up in the same movement in which Brom set it down rather than crossing ten strides of wet boot-wide coping during the first strike. The reading assembles, and the delayed provenance is arguably the stronger craft choice, so this stays in concerns.

Taste only, pre-existing and unchanged by the repair: line 13 calls the site 'two hundred meters of marsh with a drowned hall in the middle of it' while lines 21 and 29 both put the hall a hundred and seventy meters out. The two figures reconcile only if the hall is off-centre inside a two-hundred-metre perimeter that nobody has paced at this site. The r3 repair moved the hundred-and-seventy figure eight lines earlier, so the two numbers now sit closer together than they did in r2; a line-edit could harmonise them without touching anything structural.

Taste only: the line 205 trim leaves three consecutive 'said nothing' clauses (Lira, Brom, Seln) where r2 varied the third to 'said nothing at all'. The flattening is defensible as a ledger triad, but the escalation r2 had is gone and the beat is the chapter's quietest.

Taste only: 40 em dashes in 5,290 words, one more than r2 and still the highest count of any chapter drafted in the book. No charter cap governs the mark and most carry Cael's catalogue syntax, so this is not a finding.

The word band has no headroom left. At 5,290 against a ceiling of 5,290, any future line-edit that adds a single word pushes the chapter out of the packet's tolerance. Any further pass on this chapter must be net-neutral or subtractive.

Report hygiene, not a draft defect: reports/ch21-author-r3.json carries stale text from earlier revisions in three places that a downstream reader could mistake for the change manifest - obligation ED-B7CH21-004's evidence still describes 'two pre-spanned bows (Oryn's ... and Brom's ...)', and both 'inventions' and 'state_change_proposals' describe the hall as 'forty strides square' where the draft and the state entry both say twelve. The deviations block itself is accurate and matches the diff exactly.

Orchestrator note for the close: the provisional 'After Chapter 21' block in STATE_RUNNING.md still records r2's equipment staging - 'Lira two bolts one-armed from two pre-spanned bows (Oryn's, spanned by Seln at the stone; Brom's, left wound on the coping)' and 'Oryn's crossbow with Lira, re-spanned by Seln'. It must be rewritten to the single-weapon chain of custody before the chapter is spliced, or the defect this pass removed from the prose will survive in the state file.
strengths: The crossbow repair is better than a bookkeeping fix. Forcing four hits through one weapon converts a static two-bow arrangement into a timed relay - Seln spans, hands off, takes it back, spans again, keeps it - and it makes Cael's hold load-bearing in a way r2's version did not: 'because Cael held the point for as long as Seln needed and Seln knew it'. The reload is now the reason the point must be held, which is exactly the causal shape the packet's win-sentence wants. Protect this staging in any later pass.

Lira's injury is now doing work rather than being noted. She is handed the bow already spanned because she said at the stone that she could not span one and could shoot one; she braces it against the coping and her knee; she fires badly and badly is enough at four meters. One arm shapes the equipment handling, the bracing and the accuracy in three consecutive clauses.

The bent-bar repair solved a placement problem by making the observation a character's rather than the narrator's. 'Bent - by more than a hand's height, or it would not have shown at a hundred and seventy meters - ... Seln said so, and Seln's eyes were what they were' scales the evidence to the distance, keeps the viewpoint outside the line where the exception put it, and preserves the bar's load-bearing role as proof of the water-bound rule.

The four trims were taken from restatement rather than from staging, and the mechanism survived every one. 'A weight that never stopped arriving' is gone from line 61 but line 57 still carries 'pressed on it and kept pressing, and would keep pressing until he let it go'; the removal at 173 leaves 'a floor that had lied to it', which is the same finding in fewer words. The repair pass cut density without cutting legibility.

The teaching sequence is untouched and remains the chapter's best fairness work: two stone behaviours isolate settled weight from sound and from motion, the Anchor trial proves the exact interaction the climax needs, and Karis's and Cael's fixed lines still hold two mental models of one finding.

Oryn is still a healer in action rather than a fighter converted for a set piece, and the packet's restraint holds everywhere it is tested: the wyrm is neither killed nor read, the tenth fragment is spent on no one, no mind or Path is assigned to the animal, no Quieting theory is approached, and the chapter trusts dialogue after Chapter 20's log.

Pass discipline is verifiable for the first time in this chapter's history. The r2-to-r3 diff is seven lines, every one of them declared in the author report's deviations block, and the rest of the file is byte-identical. A targeted repair that can be audited this cheaply is the process working as designed.
